newsitem.title: USA: Ford unveils new 1998 Lincoln Town Car.
newsitem.headline: Ford unveils new 1998 Lincoln Town Car.

text.p: Ford Motor Co unveiled its newly designed 1998 Lincoln Town Car at the New York Auto show Wednesday, a trimmer, more agile version of the full-size luxury sedan.

The 1998 Town Car features a slightly smaller exterior, improved steering, suspension and breaks, as well as a more refined powertrain, according to Jim O'Connor, Ford Motor Co Vice President in charge of Lincoln.
O'Connor said the changes reflect a car that is more than 80 percent new from the ground up including the re-engineered, more rigid frame.
In redesigning the Town Car, Lincoln has concentrated on areas where customers have asked for improvement, Ford said.

"Our current customers were our main priority in redesigning the 1998 Town Car," said Lincoln Town Car brand mananger Mike Richards. "But we were very cognizant of how much change today's customers could accept and how much change was needed to appeal to a new customer group."

Ford said major upgrades to the 1998 Town Car include a re-engineered full perimiter steel frame, new Watt's Linkage rear suspension, refined steering gear and an optional handling package incorporating new mono-tube shock absorbers for increased firmness and improved handling feel.

The company added that tomorrow's Town Car buyer is looking for many of the same attributes in a luxury car as current Lincoln customers, but generally have more specific, more demanding desires than previous Lincoln owners.
"The new Town Car has a lot of attitude and spirit that new customers will like," O'Connor said.
The Town Car's "new, refined driving experience, powerful new looks and quality is sure to appeal to buyers who never before would have considered a Lincoln," Richards said.
